title: The Chandra test of a steady ASASSN-14ko soft floor depends on the first 2022 visit
abstract: We test whether the faint soft X-ray component of ASASSN-14ko has one detected count rate in each of 2022 and 2023. We fit 1,407 published Chandra photons with two source profiles, free companion amplitudes and a separate low-state target width. The low-state width is 1.237 times the reference width; a shared-width Poisson simulation gives p = 0.020. This small change does not establish diffuse gas. With width free, a steady low-state target rate costs 17.654 in twice log likelihood for six fewer parameters. A fitted-null Poisson simulation gives p = 0.010. Removing the first 2022 low-state visit changes the cost to 9.432 for five fewer parameters, with asymptotic p = 0.093. Thus the evidence for a variable residual depends on one short visit. The tests assume fixed source positions, a shared circular profile family and fixed backgrounds. They do not establish intrinsic residual variability, resolve covering against shutdown, or measure an orbital clock. We provide code, aggregate results, simulations, influence checks, exact input hashes and verified retrieval instructions. External photon and visit tables remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Conditional width and floor tests. The low-state rate evidence depends on the first 2022 visit; the small width increase is not a diffuse-gas detection.
